briefdescription.para: Brings the core to a known state before a transfer is launched.

detaileddescription.para: Any event latched by a previous transfer would otherwise be mistaken for an event belonging to this one. Residue left in either FIFO would be prepended to the payload. Every event is discarded rather than only completion and error. A stale threshold event is just as capable of steering the interrupt handler as a stale completion.

The core is left disabled, since writing SOFT_RESET returns every control bit to its default. Enabling it is the caller's to do, which for the driver means AmdXspi_CfgInitialize(). Anything the application configured through the option functions is returned to its default and has to be set again.
This can reach past the controller. The core passes the soft reset through to its optional resetn output. So on a design built with that output wired, the attached memory is hardware reset too.

For a HyperRAM, that returns its configuration registers, including the initial latency, to their defaults. It also costs the contents of the array, which the datasheet says to treat as lost. Anything recovering an error through AmdXspi_Abort() inherits that.
Both callers check the instance beforehand. The ready state deliberately is not checked, since AmdXspi_CfgInitialize() resets the core before marking the instance ready.

briefdescription.para: Performs a polled SPI transfer (AXI-Lite mode).

parameterdescription.para: Buffer to transmit (can be NULL for read-only).
Buffer for received data (can be NULL for write-only).

simplesect.para:
- XST_SUCCESS if transfer was successful.
XST_FAILURE if the core reported an error, stalled, or did not signal completion.
XST_DEVICE_BUSY if a transfer is in progress.

briefdescription.para: Implements the register-level functions of the AXI XSPI driver.

detaileddescription.para: This file contains the register level functions of the AXI XSPI driver. These functions operate directly on the controller registers to prepare the FIFOs for a transfer and to manage the interrupt registers.
